fix_commit.message: fix a memory leak in wasi-nn (#11704)
fix_commit.author: Masahiro Kozuka

findings.title: Tensor resources never removed from resource table in compute(), causing memory leak
findings.message: In the HostGraphExecutionContext::compute implementation, the incoming `inputs: Vec<NamedTensor>` contains `Resource<Tensor>` handles that were previously pushed into `self.table` by the guest (via a resource-creating call such as load-tensor). The compute() function iterates the inputs with `inputs.iter()` and calls `self.table.get(&tensor_resopurce)` to obtain a cloned reference to the underlying tensor. `Table::get` only borrows/clones the entry; it never removes the resource from the host resource table. Because compute() consumes the `Resource<Tensor>` handles by value (the function signature takes `inputs: Vec<NamedTensor>`, not `&Vec<NamedTensor>`), the guest loses its only handle to these resources after the call returns, yet the resources are never deleted from the host table via `self.table.delete()`. This causes each compute() call to permanently leak one table slot (and the associated backend tensor data behind it) for every input tensor, since nothing else in the code path ever calls delete/drop on these resource handles.
findings.suggestion: Consume the input resources by iterating with `into_iter()` and remove each tensor resource from the table with `self.table.delete(tensor_resource)?` instead of merely borrowing it with `self.table.get(&tensor_resource)`. This releases the table slot (and any backend memory tied to it) once the tensor has been copied out for use in compute_with_io, matching the ownership semantics implied by consuming `inputs: Vec<NamedTensor>` by value.

ground_truth.root_cause: The refactor of the wasi-nn WIT bindings (commit a7e1150019) rewrote the compute() function to iterate `inputs.iter()` and fetch tensors via `self.table.get(&tensor_resource)` (a non-consuming borrow) rather than removing them from the table, despite the function taking ownership of the `Vec<NamedTensor>` (and thus the associated Resource handles) by value. This created a mismatch between resource ownership semantics (values fully consumed by the call) and the actual table cleanup performed (none), resulting in an unbounded resource-table growth / memory leak for every compute() invocation.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Tensor resources never removed from resource table in compute(), causing memory leak
